_description: Theoretical complexity and circuit resource formulas for quantum algorithm families. Used to compute derived fields when papers don't report complexity. Every entry has a citation.

grover.citation: Grover, L.K. (1996). A fast quantum mechanical algorithm for database search. STOC 1996.
grover.notes: N = search space size. Oracle depth depends on the problem.

amplitude-estimation.citation: Brassard, G., Hoyer, P., Mosca, M., & Tapp, A. (2002). Quantum amplitude amplification and estimation. Contemporary Mathematics 305.

circuit.qubits: n_problem + ceil(log2(1/epsilon)) ancilla for phase estimation

amplitude-estimation.notes: epsilon = target precision. Used in Monte Carlo integration, derivative pricing, risk estimation.

qaoa.citation: Farhi, E., Goldstone, J., & Gutmann, S. (2014). A Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm. arXiv:1411.4028.
qaoa.classical_complexity: Problem-dependent (often O(2^N) for exact, O(poly(N)) for heuristics)

circuit.depth: O(p * N) for all-to-all; O(p * N * sqrt(N)) for 2D grid

qaoa.notes: p = QAOA depth/rounds. N = number of variables. No proven polynomial speedup over classical for general combinatorial optimization. Performance depends on problem structure and p.

vqe.citation: Peruzzo, A. et al. (2014). A variational eigenvalue solver on a photonic quantum processor. Nature Communications 5, 4213.

circuit.total_gates: O(d * N^2) for hardware-efficient; O(d * N^4) for UCCSD

vqe.notes: d = number of ansatz layers. N = number of qubits. No proven polynomial speedup for general optimization. May have advantage for specific chemistry problems.

quantum-annealing.citation: Kadowaki, T. & Nishimori, H. (1998). Quantum annealing in the transverse Ising model. Physical Review E 58(5).

circuit.qubits: N (one per binary variable in QUBO)

quantum-annealing.notes: No proven polynomial speedup over simulated annealing for general problems. Specific instances may show speedup but no general proof exists.

hhl.citation: Harrow, A.W., Hassidim, A., & Lloyd, S. (2009). Quantum algorithm for linear systems of equations. Physical Review Letters 103, 150502.

circuit.qubits: O(log(N)) for state + ancilla for phase estimation

caveats: Matrix must be sparse or efficiently row-computable — cannot load dense matrix from classical data
Solution is a quantum state — reading out full solution vector requires O(N) measurements, negating speedup
Only practical when sampling properties of solution (e.g., expectation values)
Condition number kappa must be polylog(N) for exponential speedup
hhl.notes: Exponential speedup is conditional on input/output constraints. In quantum finance: useful for structured linear systems (e.g., PDE discretizations) but NOT for general portfolio optimization.

quantum-simulation.citation: Feynman, R.P. (1982). Simulating physics with computers. International Journal of Theoretical Physics 21(6/7). Lloyd, S. (1996). Universal quantum simulators. Science 273.

circuit.qubits: N (one per simulated quantum degree of freedom)
circuit.depth: O(t * N) for Trotter; O(t * polylog(t*N/epsilon)) for qubitization

quantum-simulation.notes: Exponential speedup for simulating quantum systems. Most promising application per Hoefler. In finance: applicable when financial model maps to quantum Hamiltonian.

quantum-ml.citation: Multiple sources. Dequantization: Tang, E. (2019). A quantum-inspired classical algorithm for recommendation systems. STOC 2019.

circuit.qubits: O(log(N)) for amplitude encoding; O(N) for angle/basis encoding

caveats: Many QML speedups have been dequantized (Tang 2019)
Data loading bottleneck: encoding N classical data points requires O(N) operations
No proven general speedup for QML over classical ML
Kernel methods may have advantage for specific kernels (Liu et al. 2021)
quantum-ml.notes: No general proven speedup. Individual QML algorithms may have conditional advantages for specific problems, but dequantization results limit the scope.

quantum-svm.citation: Rebentrost, P., Mohseni, M., & Lloyd, S. (2014). Quantum support vector machine for big data classification. Physical Review Letters 113, 130503. Dequantized by Tang (2019).
quantum-svm.notes: Original exponential speedup claim was dequantized by Tang (2019). Classical algorithms with similar performance exist.

quantum-walk.citation: Szegedy, M. (2004). Quantum speed-up of Markov chain based algorithms. FOCS 2004.

circuit.qubits: O(log(N)) for graph with N nodes

quantum-walk.notes: Quadratic speedup for Markov chain problems. Used in Monte Carlo sampling. Insufficient per Hoefler.

qubo.citation: Not an algorithm but an encoding. Solved via quantum annealing (SA-01) or QAOA (SA-02).
qubo.notes: QUBO is a problem formulation, not an algorithm. Speedup depends on the solver used.

hybrid.citation: Various. Hybrid approaches combine classical and quantum subroutines.
hybrid.notes: Hybrid approaches inherit the speedup (or lack thereof) from their quantum subroutine. Assess the quantum component separately.
